Phenological retrieval error under cloud loss

cl_pheno_power.Rd

Simulates the effect of missing observations on the retrieval of phenological dates. In each replicate, a reference curve is sampled at the acquisition dates that are retained, noise is added, the curve is refitted, and the errors of the start of season, peak and end of season are recorded.

Usage

cl_pheno_power(dates, cloud_fraction = 0.4, threshold = 0.2, curve = NULL,
  noise = 0.03, n_sim = 100L, model = c("dbl_logistic", "spline"), tau = 1,
  valid_fraction = 1, retention = c("pixel", "cell"), tolerance = 5,
  persistence = NULL, seed = NULL)

Arguments

dates

Acquisition dates available in the year, in any order.

cloud_fraction

Cloud fraction for each acquisition, or a single value.

threshold

Usability threshold for retention = "cell".

curve

Function of day-of-year giving the reference trajectory, or a list of arguments passed to cl_pheno_curve.

noise

Observation noise standard deviation.

n_sim

Number of replicates.

model

Fitting model passed to cl_pheno_fit.

tau

Decorrelation time of cloud loss in days; 0 gives independent losses.

valid_fraction

Valid share of the cell for each acquisition, or a single value.

retention

"pixel" or "cell"; see the section on retention.

tolerance

Error tolerance in days for the p_within_* outputs.

persistence

Deprecated. A lag-one autocorrelation between consecutive acquisitions; converted to tau with the median interval.

seed

Random seed.

Value

A list with summary (a one-row data frame: numbers of acquisitions and retained observations, median absolute errors and median biases of start of season, peak, end of season and season length, the interquartile range of start of season, the failure and insufficient-data rates, and the p_within_* probabilities), replicates, and reference, the fit to the complete reference curve.

Which observations are retained

With retention = "pixel" (the default) each replicate is the series of a pixel at a random location in the cell. Acquisition \(i\) is observed and clear with probability \(q_i = v_i (1 - c_i)\), where \(c_i\) is the cloud fraction and \(v_i\) the valid share of the cell (1 for scene metadata, in which cloud is assumed to be spread evenly over the footprint). The expected number of retained observations is therefore \(\sum_i q_i\), the expected number of clear observations of a pixel reported by cl_clear_obs. Clear and cloudy states are drawn from a latent Gaussian process whose correlation between two acquisitions \(\Delta t\) days apart is \(\exp(-\Delta t / \tau)\): acquisition \(i\) is clear when the latent value is below \(\Phi^{-1}(q_i)\), which keeps every marginal probability exact while losses cluster in time according to the elapsed time between acquisitions. tau = 0 gives independent losses.

With retention = "cell", an acquisition is retained when at least 1 - threshold of the cell was observed and cloud-free, as in cl_clear_obs; the retained set is then the same in every replicate and only the noise varies.

Success and failure

A replicate succeeds when at least six observations are retained, the fit converges, and the fitted curve has a start of season, a peak and an end of season in that order. Errors are summarised over successful replicates. Because errors conditional on success can look small when most replicates fail, p_within_* report the probability, over all replicates, that the replicate succeeded and the error of that date was at most tolerance days; p_within_all requires all three dates to be within it.

Examples

d <- seq(as.Date("2023-01-01"), as.Date("2023-12-31"), by = "10 days")
r <- cl_pheno_power(d, cloud_fraction = 0.5, n_sim = 30, seed = 1)
r$summary[, c("n_retained_median", "sos_mae", "failure_rate", "p_within_all")]
#>   n_retained_median sos_mae failure_rate p_within_all
#> 1              18.5     1.6          0.2          0.2
